status_reason: The enquiry asks for a surgical decision on brain tumour patients, which needs validation beyond a first assessment; no supplied source contains brain tissue data, and the closest application (kidney, chicken and model tissue) is research-stage only.
answer: The supplied sources do not support naming a system for deciding which brain tissue to remove. A first step is a laboratory test of a combined MIR ATR and fluorescence fiber probe on brain tumour and normal tissue, compared with NIR alone on the same spots. The multispectral camera option rests on external imaging research and is not evidence for an in-line fiber method.

inline.headline: Test MIR ATR + fluorescence combined probe on brain tumour and normal tissue in the lab before any surgical use
inline.probe: combined ZrO2 ATR head with an IR fiber and a fluorescence fiber, so both methods see the same spot
inline.install: Not in the operating room yet; lab bench first. Surgical use would only be considered after validation, with the probe tip in direct contact with tissue as described in the application concept
inline.fiber: PIR fiber (3-16 µm) for the MIR ATR leg; silica fiber (190-1200 nm) for the fluorescence leg
inline.test_against: NIR reflection probe alone, on the same tissue spots
inline.not_final_because: No brain tissue data in the sources; the tested tissue was chicken and model tissue; fluorescence needs a fluorescent component; the approach is limited to ATR-suitable samples; frozen or thawed samples may differ from in vivo tissue; measurement variance in cancer tissue was very high in the kidney study.

problems.text: No source tests brain tumours. The data cover chicken, model tissue and kidney biopsies, and the surgical margin concept has no validation data.
Using two separate probes in turn cannot guarantee that both methods measure the same spot, and alternating measurements cannot be used in clinical surgery. A combined probe is needed.
Fluorescence only works if the tissue has a fluorescent component, and the ATR approach only suits liquids and soft solids. Brain tissue suitability is unknown.
The multispectral camera is an external imaging research device, not an AFS fiber system, and its sources give no tissue validation for a surgical decision.

methods.why: A combined probe for tumour margin and tissue classification was built and tested on model tissue, and the same pair classified chicken tissue where neither method alone did in PCA.
NIR is the most common online fiber-probe method and penetrates several millimetres, so it is the single-method comparison.
Raman with 785 nm excitation adds molecular backbone information, but its signals are weak and can be masked by fluorescence, so it is only needed if the first pair fails.
The camera sources are external imaging research with no AFS fiber evidence and no tissue validation for the surgical decision.

questions.q: What exact decision must the surgeon make at the margin, and what false-negative rate is acceptable?
questions.why: Without a target, no method can be judged; false negatives are unacceptable in oncology.

questions.q: Which tissue samples can you provide for lab tests, and are they fresh or frozen?
questions.why: Frozen and thawed biopsies can differ from in vivo measurements, which changes the test design.

questions.q: Will the probe contact the tissue directly during surgery, and what access route is planned?
questions.why: Direct tip contact sets the probe design and the fiber choice.

questions.q: What reference method will confirm tumour and normal tissue, and how many samples and points are available?
questions.why: Reference measurements must be independent laboratory analyses, and the sample count sets the validation design.

experiment.objective: Test whether combined MIR ATR and fluorescence beats the best single method on brain tumour and normal tissue measured at the same spots.
steps: Obtain tumour and normal brain tissue samples from the client and record whether each is fresh, frozen or thawed.
Build a combined ZrO2 ATR probe with a PIR fiber to the MIR spectrometer and a silica fiber to the fluorescence spectrometer.
Measure tissue pairs at the same points, using a design of 3 samples per tissue with 5 points each as in the chicken study.
Compare PCA separation of fused spectra with MIR-only and fluorescence-only models on the same data.
Validate with independent laboratory reference analysis and segmented cross-validation with randomisation tests.
references: S04 p.1-4: combined ATR-MIR and fluorescence probe, same-spot design and fused PCA result
S03 p.14: validation requirements for limited data
experiment.go_no_go: Criteria come from the client; none were given in the enquiry.

pathway.key_features: To be identified from the lab spectra; in the chicken study the candidate bands were the ester carbonyl near 1740 cm-1, amide I and II near 1640 and 1548 cm-1, and the FAD fluorescence band at 520-530 nm, which may not transfer to brain tissue.
pathway.path_reason: The concept has no brain tissue validation, so a lab test must come first.

multispectral.why: MIR gives molecular fingerprint bands of fat and protein, while fluorescence detects intracellular FAD and porphyrin signals; the pair gives complementary information, and the fused data separated tissue classes that neither method separated alone.
multispectral.test: On the same validation spots, compare the fused model with MIR-only and fluorescence-only models; the combination is only accepted if it beats the best single method.

assumptions: The target is brain tumour tissue at the surgical margin.
Tissue samples can be obtained for laboratory tests.
The hospital wants a decision at the margin, not a finished product.
Tissue behaviour in brain may differ from the chicken and kidney studies.
